no_changes_rationale:
status: blocked
reason: The 100k/1M/10M hybrid-async release tiers cannot pass the hot-path gate on this shared execution host; a provisioned/dedicated perf host is required. AC1 (100k) fails reproducibly (3/3 runs, exit 101): hybrid ack_p99-vs-inmemory ratio 1.736 / 2.115 / 3.176 (all > 1.20 gate); claim/finalize p95 ratio swings 0.30–3.09, characteristic of shared-host tail contention. This is NOT a timing/disk failure — object logs write to $TMPDIR on /dev/vdb1 (288G free) and each run finishes in ~11s. The durability/correctness gates (recovery, disk-loss reconstruction, bounded apply-debt, segment density, attribution) all pass at 100k; only the "hybrid hot path within 20% of pure in-memory objectlog" latency bar fails. This matches the prior evidence doc, which already documents 100k+ requires a provisioned perf host and that this host's capacity is 10k (docs/perf/tp002-objectlog-hybrid-evidence.md:94,205). AC2 (1M) and AC3 (10M) are strictly larger, exercise the same gate, and would cost 20–40x the wall time to reconfirm the known failure, so they were not run. Full evidence: .ddx/executions/20260701T212322-823b6b4b/hybrid-scale-release-blocker.md. The committed 10k-pass hybrid-scale ledger was restored (no source/production code changed). Unblock: run on an isolated perf host, and/or a design decision on the hybrid claim/finalize scaling characteristic vs the inmemory-parity bar for durable backends at release scale (code change, out of this bead's scope).
